summary: Douglas County, OR lookout on Anderson Mountain, Umpqua NF; built 1933-34 as an L-5 cab, abandoned in the 1950s, later burned. In 2018 only footings and some wooden legs remained.

facts.status_note: Tower was later destroyed by burning; a 2018 visit found only the footings and some wooden support legs.

access.note: Reached on foot over Forest Service trails; the 2018 hike report describes no closure or permit requirement.

visit.trail_note: Park at the Forest Road 6515 trailhead, take the Anderson Camp Trail (USFS 1075) to the Rogue-Umpqua Divide, then go south on the Divide Trail (USFS 1470). The first trail gets limited maintenance and the trees now block the view.

events.note: Roseburg newspaper notice said a 10x10 lookout was to be built before the snow flew
2018 hike report gives 1933 as the year the 30-foot pole live-in tower was built
L-5 lookout cab built atop a 30-foot round timber tower by the Civilian Conservation Corps (Forest Lookouts); firelookout.com also gives 1934 but a 10-foot pole tower
Four-strand barbed wire fence enclosing 20 acres built at a cost of $30.29
Louis Gable stationed at Anderson Camp during the summer months, per a News-Review notice
2018 report and firelookout.com give 1958; Forest Lookouts says abandoned about mid-decade

notes_for_editor: Gone. The 2018 hike report is the only source that describes the site now; it is a single blog visit, so treat the footings detail as 2018 only. Build year conflicts: 1933 (2018 report and the Sept 1933 plan) vs 1934 (Forest Lookouts, firelookout.com); left as a conflict. Abandonment: 1958 (2018 report, firelookout.com) vs mid-1950s (Forest Lookouts). Height: 30 ft (9.1 m, matching the record) per the 2018 report and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says '10' pole L-5 tower', which we did not use. Not verified: whether the record's coordinates (42.97805, -122.47775) mark the lookout on Anderson Mountain or the Anderson Camp meadow; the FFLA entry uses the Anderson Camp name. Access level 'public' is inferred from the 2018 hike on Forest Service trails, and no closure, permit or closed wording on the full 2018 page; no official site access statement was read. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads (within budget). No photos used: the 2018 blog photos have no stated licence, and firelookout.com credits a private collection.
